title: Spectral clustering and graph Laplacians
summary: Move from a graph adjacency matrix to Laplacian eigenvectors, relaxed cuts, and a clustering embedding.
objectives: Form D and L from a graph

sections.title: Reference depth · Laplacian construction
sections.body: For an undirected graph with adjacency matrix $A$, define degree matrix $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)$ and unnormalized Laplacian $L=D-A$. The normalized variants use $D^{-\frac{1}{2}}LD^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ or a related random-walk form.

math.explanation: The diagonal counts incident edge weight and the off-diagonal adjacency subtracts connections. Each row of L sums to zero for the unnormalized Laplacian.
math.name: Graph Laplacian
math.purpose: Use it to encode degree minus adjacency and prepare the spectral relaxation of a cut problem.

sections.title: Reference depth · Smoothness and cuts
sections.body: For a symmetric graph, $f^\top Lf=\frac12\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}(f_i-f_j)^2$. A low value means connected nodes receive similar scalar values. The constant vector is the zero-eigenvalue direction; the next eigenvector, often called the Fiedler vector for a connected graph, gives a relaxed two-way partition signal.

math.explanation: The quadratic form turns graph connectivity into an energy. Spectral clustering relaxes a discrete cut problem into an eigenvector problem, then clusters rows of the selected eigenvector embedding.

symbols.meaning: edge weight between i and j

math.name: Laplacian smoothness identity
math.purpose: Use it to connect a quadratic form with disagreement across graph edges and the quality of a partition.

sections.title: Reference depth · Spectral-clustering pipeline
sections.body: Build an affinity graph, choose a Laplacian, compute the smallest non-trivial eigenvectors, use their rows as an embedding, and run K-means in that embedding. The final K-means step is a separate approximation; spectral eigenvectors do not themselves assign arbitrary cluster names.

sections.title: Assessment habit · Link the objects
sections.body: If asked for a Laplacian eigenvector, write the matrix before the eigendecomposition. If asked for a clustering interpretation, explain why smooth eigenvectors separate weakly connected groups. If asked for a numerical eigenvector, remember its sign and scale can be chosen by convention.

examples.title: Path graph with three nodes
steps: The remaining eigenvectors vary across the path; the lowest non-constant one changes slowly and can be thresholded to form a two-way partition.
examples.answer: The Laplacian encodes disagreement across edges, not a generic dense covariance matrix.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Why does the Laplacian quadratic form encourage smoothness?
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: It is a sum of edge-weighted squared differences. Large disagreement across a strong edge costs more, so low-energy vectors vary slowly along connected regions.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Why is K-means still present after the eigenvectors?
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Spectral analysis creates a geometry-aware embedding; K-means is then used to assign embedded points to clusters. These are distinct stages with distinct objectives.
